Senses.Explanation: Before the Stupa of Many Sons — the spot the tradition fixes for the first handing-over, and the emblem Chan rows reach for whenever a robe moves, an heir is weighed, or the old news is raised once more. Yuanwu Keqin, opening the hall for the invited elder of Changlu: before the Stupa of Many Sons the half-seat was shared, the stream cut off; at Shaolin nine years seated still, a wall of ten-thousand fathoms — rousing the smith's bellows, applying the upward tongs, the great function and great machine wholly alive and wholly killing, drawing nails and stripping glue for everyone; and Mi'an Xianjie, at the sovereign's birthday: the forest-dweller — how shall he repay the grace? The news before the Stupa of Many Sons stands; each time it is raised, it is new. Hanyue Fazang, raising the robe his own teacher at Jinsu had sent: ever since before the Stupa of Many Sons it wrapped Kasyapa, he has sat cold to this day before Cockfoot Peak; in the room at Huangmei it fenced the Sixth Patriarch, and under the horse's hooves the bustle has not stopped — and today it is handed on down the generations to the hall of Quiet Rest, and on close inspection is only good for wrapping a thirty-year-old broken straw sandal; Yongjue Yuanxian, at a layman's robe-gift: before the Stupa of Many Sons, the pillars and the lanterns butt heads; at midnight in Huangmei, the black cat and the white calf cross in study — just at that moment, what was handed over? He lifts the corner of the kasaya: not woven by the Weaver Maid, but all the mother-of-change's loom; one thread running through, and it can shade heaven and cover earth; truly not an inch of silk hung, and then it may range seven ways and eight. Juelang Daosheng, sending the warden-layman into the room: the Tathagata of Jinsu once occupied this room, today the coast re-raises the line's wind — and closes: before the Stupa of Many Sons he knows my nobility; outside the night-lit curtain the king of the teaching is honored — take care! Baichi Xingyuan, at the hall held for the patron praying for an heir: the news before the Stupa of Many Sons stands; one raising, one renewal — then raises the old case, the monk asking Xinghua: before the Stupa of Many Sons, what was to be discussed? One man passes on emptiness, ten thousand pass it on as fact — the master stamps him: the ready sword of life-and-death, that old man of Xinghua; and Yuanjie Ying, at the decade-memorial handing the robe to the elder of the west hall: before the Stupa of Many Sons it was never finished; the handing-on has gone round until today — this mountain monk with both hands gives it over in person: five petals, one flower, spring across the great earth. And the scene that set the standard: Baiyu Jingsi's lineage-source cycle retells the fourteenth patriarch Tongan Guanzhi attending the earlier Tongan — Tongan Daopi at the point of death ascending the hall: before the Stupa of Many Sons the true heir shows; before Five Elders Peak, how stands the matter? Asked three times, none answered — then the master came out: outside the night-lit curtain, standing in rank; ten thousand miles of song proclaim the great peace. The dying one said: it had to be this blind fellow. Baiyu's own verse on it: the old man never resting his mind, alas — teaching his boy to busy himself keeping house.
